About: Length Contraction & Simultaneity

Source

Lecture
11 — Special Relativity: Length contraction
Section
§b — Length contraction as a consequence of the relativity of simultaneity
Concept
The moving rod's shorter length in Alice's frame is the direct arithmetic consequence of her two "same-instant" endpoint marks not being simultaneous in Bella's frame.
Serves
Deriving L = L₀/γ; connecting length contraction to the relativity of simultaneity; the worked answer L = 0.6 m at v = 0.8c, L₀ = 1 m.
Misconception
That the moving rod is "really" shorter, or that two events simultaneous in one frame are simultaneous in every frame.

Welcome toLength Contraction & Simultaneity

A rod is carried past at a good fraction of light speed. Marking where both of its ends are, at one instant, is where the trouble starts.

Guided Inquiry

1 · Measuring a rod that is moving

Here’s the puzzle. Bella carries a rod of rest length L₀ past Alice at speed v; the rod is at rest in Bella’s frame, so she can read L₀ at her leisure. Alice, who sees it moving, has no such luxury: she has to locate both ends at the same instant of her own time. And “at the same instant”, as you’ll see, is a statement about a frame.

2 · What Alice's two marks give

Let’s start with Alice. The rod’s rest length is L₀ = 1 m and it passes at v = 0.8c. Alice marks where each end is at one instant of her time, then measures the distance between the two marks. How do you think that distance compares with L₀?

Now switch to Alice’s frame and press Measure — Alice to see it for yourself.

3 · The same marks, seen by Bella

Now let’s look at those marks through Bella’s eyes. Alice’s two marks are made at one instant of her own time. In Bella’s frame, what do you think — do those two marking events still happen at the same instant?

Switch to Bella’s frame and watch closely: the two marks fire at different times.

4 · What happens to the rod itself

So here’s where we are. Alice’s pair of marks is 0.60 m apart. Bella, marking both ends at one instant of her own time, gets 1.00 m for the same rod. What do you think is happening to the rod itself?

Go ahead and press Measure — Bella, then read L in her frame.

5 · How the result scales with speed

One last experiment. The same rod of rest length L₀ is now carried past Alice at v = 0.6c instead of 0.8c. Make a guess — what fraction of L₀ do her two marks enclose now?

Try it: set v/c to 0.60 and read L against L₀.

6 · Contraction is simultaneity, applied to a ruler

Let’s pull it all together. L = L₀/γ is neither a separate postulate nor a force: measuring a moving object means locating both ends at once, and “at once” belongs to a frame, so observers who disagree about simultaneity must disagree about length. The rest-frame length L₀ is the longest any observer finds, and only the dimension along the motion shrinks.

γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²) · L = L₀/γ
Δt′ = −γ v Δx/c² — Alice's simultaneous marks, timed by Bella

The Physics

Length contraction and simultaneity · what this sim shows, the physics behind it, and every control

01

At a glance

Two observers, Alice and Bella, each mark the two ends of the same rod and compare what they record. The sim shows how a length depends on when its ends are located, and how that depends on the frame.

What you'll learn

  • How a length is measured when the object is moving, and which two events it needs.
  • How the timing of those two events looks from a second frame.
  • How the measured length depends on the speed v and the rest length L₀.
  • Which quantities the two observers agree on.
Bella carries the rod past Alice at speed v. The dashed lines mark the two ends.

03

How a length gets measured

A length is the distance between two ends. That is simple for a rod at rest, and needs care for a rod that moves, because its ends keep moving while you measure.

Two ways to fix the two ends, one for each observer.
  • Bella's frame. The rod is at rest, so its ends stay put. She can read them at any times and subtract. This gives the rest length L₀.
  • Alice's frame. The ends move, so she must locate both of them at one instant of her own time, t₁ = t₂, and then subtract.
  • Events. Each mark is an event with a position and a time. A time coordinate is what a clock at that event reads, so light-travel delay is not part of it.
See itLet Alice mark both ends at one instant of her time. Watch for: t₁ and t₂ in Readouts matching, so Δt reads 0.00 (simultaneous).
04

Alice's marks give L = L₀/γ

Bella moves at +v relative to Alice, so Alice's coordinates (t, x) and Bella's (t′, x′) are related by the Lorentz transformation:

The course's transformation. Bella moves at +v in Alice's frame.

Alice's marks have t₁ = t₂, so the vt terms cancel when you subtract the two x′ values. Those marks sit on the rod's ends, and in Bella's frame the ends are L₀ apart:

The derivation: put t₁ = t₂ into x′ = γ(x − vt).
The rest length L₀ is the longest any observer finds.
v / c L₀

These sliders move the sim too.

  • The speed enters only through γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²), so L is not linear in v. γ is 1.15 at 0.5c, 1.67 at 0.8c and 7.09 at 0.99c.
  • The formula applies to a length along the direction of motion, which is how the sim places the rod.
See itSet v = 0.95c with L₀ = 1.00 m and let Alice mark the ends. Watch for: L reading about 0.31 m, while L₀ stays 1.00 m.
05

Simultaneity depends on the frame

Alice's two marks have Δt = 0 and Δx = L. Put that into the time equation of the transformation:

Simultaneous for Alice, staggered for Bella.
  • Not simultaneous for Bella. Δt′ = t′₂ − t′₁ is not zero. It is negative, so the front mark E₂ happens first in her frame.
  • The sim's numbers. At v = 0.8c and L₀ = 1 m, Δt′ = −0.80 m of light (about 2.67 ns). In Bella's frame the t₁, t₂ and Δt rows show t′₁ = +0.40, t′₂ = −0.40 and Δt′ = −0.80.
  • Not a light delay. The stagger grows with the speed and with the separation L. It is already a statement about clock readings at the events.
See itView Alice's two marks from Bella's frame. Watch for: the marks firing one after the other, and Δt turning amber with Δt ≠ 0.
06

No force squeezes the rod

  • Bella reads L₀ at every speed. In her frame the rod is at rest and nothing about it changes. L₀ is also the longest length any observer finds.
  • Two different pairs of events. Alice's marks and Bella's marks are not the same events. L and L₀ answer different questions, and each is correct in its own frame.
  • The effect is reciprocal. Bella finds that an identical rod, at rest in Alice's frame, is shortened by the same factor γ. Neither frame is privileged.

What changes with the frame is the measured length. The rod itself is not compressed.

See itLet Bella mark her own rod at v = 0.95c. Watch for: L reading 1.00 m, equal to L₀, although γ is 3.203.
07

The interval is the same in both frames

The sim and the course use the sign convention Δs² = −c²Δt² + Δx². With c = 1 and lengths in metres, Δs² = −Δt² + Δx², in m².

Frames split the interval differently into time and distance. They agree on its value.
  • Alice: Δt = 0 and Δx = L = 0.60 m, so Δs² = 0.36 m².
  • Bella: Δt′ = −0.80 m and Δx′ = 1.00 m, so Δs² = −0.64 + 1.00 = 0.36 m². These are the sim's opening values.
  • Spacelike. Δs² > 0 means no signal can connect the two marks, so their order can differ between frames. That is why Δt′ can be negative.
See itShow Alice's two marks as events on Bella's spacetime diagram. Watch for: the card giving Δx′, Δt′ and a Δs² equal to Alice's L².
08

Where it matters

A sphere at three speeds, as measured: only the dimension along the motion shrinks.
  • Cosmic-ray muons. At γ ≈ 20, the 15 km of atmosphere above a muon is about 750 m long in the muon's frame, short enough for it to cross before it decays.
  • Heavy ions at the LHC. Lead nuclei run at γ ≈ 2700, so in the lab a nucleus is about 2700 times thinner along the beam than at rest.
  • Everyday speeds. A 60 m airliner at 200 m/s is shortened by about 10⁻¹¹ m, around a tenth of an atom's width.
Go deeper: measured shape and photographed shape

Contraction describes the shape found by locating every point at one instant of a frame. A camera records light that left different points at different times, so a fast sphere is photographed as a circle, not a flattened ellipse.

09

Summary

In one line. A moving rod's length is found by locating both ends at one instant of an observer's time. Observers in relative motion disagree about "one instant", so they get different lengths, L = L₀/γ for the observer the rod moves past.

Key points

  • L₀ is the length in the rod's own frame. It is the longest any observer finds.
  • Alice's two simultaneous marks are not simultaneous for Bella: Δt′ = −γvL/c².
  • The speed enters only through γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²).
  • The interval Δs² = −c²Δt² + Δx² is the same in both frames.

Common mix-ups

  • "A force squeezes the moving rod." No force acts. Alice and Bella measure different pairs of events.
  • "The marks are staggered because light takes time to arrive." The times are clock readings at the events. The stagger comes from the Lorentz transformation.
  • "Only Alice finds a contraction." It is reciprocal: each observer finds the other's moving rod shorter.

Things to try on your own

  • Set v/c to 0.6, let Alice mark the ends, and compare L with L₀/γ.
  • Set L₀ = 1.6 m at v = 0.8c, switch to Bella's frame, and check Δt against −γvL/c².
  • Find the speed at which L is half of L₀, then compare it with c√3/2 ≈ 0.866c.
